text:
Marta L: Heads up — after the batching tweak rolled yesterday we started seeing regressions for mixed short/long workloads. p95 latency for tenant-gamma spikes ~120ms on steady traffic.

Oliver K: Can you paste the profiler output / a quick flame?

Marta L: Pasting the condensed profiler snapshot from the canary host:
```
profile_summary:
p50 18ms, p95 420ms
hot_spans: kernel_selection (37%), kv-miss-stall (23%), batch_serialize (12%)
kernel_table_hits: generic_fp16=72%, int8_opt=18%, fallback_cpu=10%
observed: long requests (>1024) cause KV miss ripple and batch coalescing waits
```

Sam R: Sounds like long requests are occupying the batch head while the batcher continues filling to token_budget. Short requests pile up behind — classic head-of-line impact.

Tia P: Proposal sketch: slot-reservation allocator rather than pure token-fill. Each lane gets a small number of "slots" per refill cycle; long sequences can consume multiple slots (adaptive), shorts get minimum 1 slot to keep latency low.

Jordan M: How would we pick slot sizes and refill cadence? We need adaptive targets driven by observed seq-length distribution + KV hit rate.

Anya S: Telemetry shows tenancy skew: tenant-alpha ~80% <=64 tokens, tenant-gamma ~55% >=1024. Per-tenant targets would help — otherwise gamma dominates shared queues.

infra-bot: Canary deployment starting: batcher-v2-slot-reserve on hosts a3..a6 (rollout 10%)

Oliver K: Also adjust kernel selection heuristics: if a mini-batch composition has >50% long-token work, prefer int8 optimized kernel for that batch to reduce memory bandwidth and avoid CPU fallback. Our current selector biases fp16 which increases KV pressure.

Marta L: Config sketch (for discussion):
```json
{
  "batcher": {
    "refill_interval_ms": 5,
    "slots_per_refill": 8,
    "slot_size_tokens": 64,
    "long_seq_multiplier": 4,
    "aging_threshold_ms": 30
  },
  "kernel_selector": {
    "prefer_int8_when_long_ratio_gt": 0.5,
    "fallback_to_cpu_ms": 200
  },
  "per_tenant_profiles": {
    "tenant-gamma": { "min_slots": 2 },
    "tenant-alpha": { "min_slots": 1 }
  }
}
```

Sam R: Important: add an "aging" bump — if a request sits > aging_threshold_ms, it gets priority escalation for the next refill (prevents indefinite wait).

Tia P: I'll add a simulator case: 80/20 short/long arrival mix, kv_hit=0.3, burst load, run 30m to steady-state. Need to capture p50/p95 for both short and long lanes, batch sizes, kernel-switch rate, and kv-miss latency.

Jordan M: If sim looks good, rollout plan: canary 5% -> 20% -> 50% with automated rollback on p95 increase >10% or kernel-fallback-rate increase >2pp.

Anya S: Also evaluate pinning hot KV keys for enterprise tenants (reduces remote misses). This is orthogonal but could dramatically lower kv-miss stall for heavy long-seq tenants.

Oliver K: I'll run a microbenchmark to quantify kernel-switch overhead (ms per switch) and effect on batch formation latency; that will inform prefer_int8_when_long_ratio threshold.

Marta L: Thanks. @Sam R @Tia P can you own the sim harness? I'll open an RFC with the config above and a short measurement plan.

Sam R: Yep — taking it. :thumbsup:

Tia P: On it — will post sim results in this thread. :mag_right:

deploy-bot: Canary deployment succeeded on hosts a3,a4 (10% traffic).

Marta L: Great. If we can keep short-lane p95 within 5% and reduce long-lane tail, this approach looks promising. We'll iterate on slot sizes and aging.

Oliver K: One more thought — expose an opt-in per-tenant "latency sensitivity" flag so customers can pick strict short-latency behavior vs throughput-optimized mixes.

Anya S: That would be useful for enterprise SLAs.

Marta L: Cool. I'll include that in the RFC. Closing loop after sims.
